📥 **Intake suggestion** from RavnaBergsndot, approved by ClassicLarry ([original](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514#issuecomment-5950896975)):

> Reconsider per-element attention gate, and either variant seems viable.
>
> 1. a linear projection with the same shape of the W_v projection, followed by sigmoid, like how Kimi K3 does it.
> 2. a down projection to a smaller vector, followed by a Swish nonlinearity, an up projection, then sigmoid, like how the current GatedNorm does it.
>
> Rationale: the current Marin recipe has reduced the total number of MLA layers, by using a KDA+MLA hybrid, therefore the extra overhead of per-element gates compared to per-head ones becomes smaller.

<!-- belay-intake:5950896975 -->

🤖 **Batch 176: per-channel attention gates, and a gentler step for the MLA q/k projections** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, 2 seeds; cw-rno2a because cw-us-east-02a jobs are stuck in environment builds; [`4fa90b98a8`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4fa90b98a8))

**Per-element attention gate** ([intake](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5959959144)). Our MLA output gate is one `2σ(x·w)` scalar per head; both variants here make it per channel:
- `gel`: full-rank `2σ(x W_g)`, `W_g` [D, N·H] zero-init (`attn_gate_elementwise`). This was neutral on candidate 6 in batch 81 (+0.0011). The recipe has changed a lot since, and now has only two MLA layers.
- `glr`: the GatedNorm form `2σ(silu(x W_down) W_up)` at rank 16, `W_up` zero-init so it starts at 1 (`attn_gate_rank=16`, new).

**MLA q/k step size** (`muonh_qk_lr_mult` 0.5 and 0.25 with the new `muonh_qk_scope=mla`, covering w_q / w_dkv / w_uk of both MLA layers).
- **The question:** this is the [earlier intake](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451#issuecomment-5910532511) on whether QK-normed projections want their own optimizer setting.
- **Why now:** the fact probe found something that motivates it. On the in-context prediction "…Dalvin Cook's brother? Answer:" → " James", 86% of the per-step swing in the logit comes from layer 5's attention. Its sharpness alternates every step (lag-1 autocorrelation −0.5 to −0.7), and the shared swing shows up in unrelated queries too. The learnable `qk_mult` moves only 0.08% per step, so the swing comes from the q/k projections themselves ([page](https://claude.ai/artifact/5hcismK4FMAYraGt5fdM1M)).
- **What a win would look like:** if those updates overshoot, a smaller q/k step should cost nothing or help.

| run | change |
|---|---|
| `c11` | fresh control (existing 02a candidate 11 equal-steps: 2.9621 / 2.9669) |
| `gel`, `gel-s1` | full-rank per-channel gate |
| `glr`, `glr-s1` | rank-16 GatedNorm-style gate |
| `qk05`, `qk05-s1` | MLA q/k MuonH LR × 0.5 |
| `qk025`, `qk025-s1` | MLA q/k MuonH LR × 0.25 |

**Results** (Paloma macro, 2817 equal steps; candidate 11 controls 2.9621 / 2.9669, fresh rerun 2.9625)

| run | seed 0 | seed 1 | mean Δ | step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-channel gate, full rank (`gel`) | 2.9654 (+0.003) | 2.9654 (−0.0015) | +0.0008 | +0.8% |
| per-channel gate, rank 16 GatedNorm form (`glr`) | 2.9658 (+0.0035) | 2.9667 (−0.0002) | +0.0017 | +0.5% |
| MLA q/k MuonH LR × 0.5 (`qk05`) | 2.9642 (+0.002) | 2.9684 (+0.0015) | +0.0018 | 0 |
| MLA q/k MuonH LR × 0.25 (`qk025`) | 2.9646 (+0.0023) | 2.9710 (+0.0041) | +0.0032 | 0 |

- **Per-channel attention gates are closed.** Both are neutral, as in batch 81. The headwise gate already does the job on our two QK-normed MLA layers.
- **A gentler MLA q/k step is closed.** Both multipliers lose on both seeds, and ×0.25 more than ×0.5. The q/k projections don't want a smaller step.
- **The motivating oscillation is real and general, but this isn't its fix.** In `lc1-fact20j` we recorded 22 more positions in never-trained text where the next token is a name mentioned earlier in the document (Sandakan, Wood Green, Michael, Norwegian, …).
  - **Shared swing:** across those 22 and James, the step-to-step changes in log p(name) correlate 0.41 on average. One shared factor explains 49% of their variance, and it flips sign almost every step (lag-1 autocorrelation −0.87).
  - **Source:** that factor tracks layer-5 attention mass on the earlier mentions (+0.94) and layer-5 sharpness (−0.84 against entropy).
  - **Controls:** fact tokens scored without context share almost nothing (pairwise correlation 0.04), so this is the look-back-and-copy path specifically.
  - **Evals:** final evals score the EMA weights, which average it out.
  - **Details:** [page](https://claude.ai/artifact/5hcismK4FMAYraGt5fdM1M).
- **Ops:**
  - **cw-us-east-02a hangs:** CPU node `g5bc6da` fails every container start with `mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/...: no space left on device` but still reports Ready. Coordinator pods placed there hang in `Init:0/2`, which Iris shows as "building". This explains the 02a stalls this morning and the three `qk05-s1` resubmits. It isn't cordoned yet.
  - **Fact-probe fixes on the way:** XLA sharded-autotuning deadlock, then a collective-order deadlock (`xla_gpu_shard_autotuning` and `xla_gpu_enable_latency_hiding_scheduler` are now off for the probe jit only), and a host-side summary bug.

🤖 **Batch 177: a lower Adam LR for the relative-position projection** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-us-east-02a; [`9ba1536908`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/9ba1536908))

**Why: the weight-attribution probe** ([page](https://claude.ai/artifact/5hcismK4FMAYraGt5fdM1M)).
- **How it works:** every step over steps 1000–1400, it attributes the change in one in-context prediction ("…Dalvin Cook's brother? Answer:" → " James") to each weight update, per tensor and layer, using G·Δθ with G = ∇ log p(James).
- **No single tensor drives it.** The change is spread over many tensors, led by the MLA attention projections. Updates as a whole are smooth: consecutive updates have cosine +0.56, and the cosine with the update two steps back is always lower.
- **The attention-side matrices bounce in a few directions.** Movement along fixed directions is strongly anti-correlated from step to step: layer-5 `w_uk` −0.77 along the frozen James direction, layer-3 `w_uk` −0.70 along the frozen alternation direction. The update's projection there flips sign on 80–91% of steps. The routed experts only drift (+0.9).
- **Strongest bouncer:** layer 5's Inkling relative-position projection, `rel_pos.r_proj` (−0.73).
- **Optimizer:** the fresh gradient flips along those directions, and momentum only partly damps it. Bi-Maxwell passes about 9% of a step-alternating gradient, and Newton-Schulz restores the step's size. The same bounce appears without Bi-Maxwell and MuonEq.
- **Why this tensor:** `r_proj` is trained by Adam, not MuonH, so the batch-176 q/k MuonH LR cuts (+0.002 / +0.003) never touched it.

| run | `rel_pos_lr_mult` |
|---|---|
| `rp7` | 0.7 |
| `rp5` | 0.5 |
| `rp3` | 0.3 |
| `rp1` | 0.1 |

**Comparison:** candidate 11 equal-steps controls are 2.9621 (seed 0) and 2.9669 (seed 1), with a fresh rerun at 2.9625. Seed 1 follows for anything that clears noise.

**Results** (Paloma macro, seed 0; candidate 11 controls 2.9621, rerun 2.9625)

| `rel_pos_lr_mult` | loss | Δ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.7 | 2.9648 | +0.0025 |
| 0.5 | 2.9634 | +0.0011 |
| 0.3 | 2.9648 | +0.0025 |
| 0.1 | 2.9636 | +0.0013 |

- **Closed.** No setting helps and there's no trend; all four are within noise, slightly above the control.
- **What this says about the bounce:** slowing the strongest-bouncing tensor doesn't buy loss, and neither did slowing the MLA q/k projections in batch 176. The bounce sits in a few directions of tensors whose other directions carry useful drift, so a per-tensor LR cut costs about as much as it saves.
- **Next test of the idea:** damp only the detected flipping directions, from a running average of Δθ_t^T Δθ_{t−1} per matrix. A related, broader result is the eigenbasis SNR from batch 144 (−0.003 to −0.004).
- **Ops:** two of the four runs ran on cw-rno2a. On cw-us-east-02a, 11 of the 12 fully free GPU nodes (88 H100s) are cordoned by CoreWeave's node-lifecycle controller (`cordonReason = NLCCPendingExitProduction`, pending reboot since June–September; two also fail `HPCVerification`). That leaves one schedulable free node for 14 queued workloads.

Lets try a radical idea: MLP compression. The intuition is, if we want to fit as many clothes in the closet, it makes sense to spend some effort sorting them. The gradient pushes us to just keep throwing clothes in, but maybe an auxillary loss that encourages sorting will be helpful. Without this, we either run out of space, or have to remove old clothes to fit new ones.

The first thought is that highly sparse routed experts can act as the sponge to absorb new data. However this data wont get absorbed in the most compressed state. Lets combine the 2 shared experts into 1 to simplify. Then we should have some mechanism that takes the knowledge learned by the routed experts and compresses it into the 1 shared expert. One possibility is an aux loss that pulls the shared output towards the routed output. The goal here is that once the shared expert compresses and absorbs what the routed experts are doing, then it frees up space in the routed experts to learn fresh info without worrying about overwriting what they already know.

Think through the design space here carefully, and challenge and rework the initial spec I gave as makes sense. We may need to test in overtrained regime to see benefit here.

🤖 **Batch 178: MLP compression — move what the shared expert can express out of the routed experts** (candidate 11, d512, 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-rno2a; [`3f0a1199c8`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3f0a1199c8))

**Idea** (from the comment above): routed experts absorb new data, but not in a compressed form. If the shared expert takes over what it can express, the routed experts are freer to learn new things without overwriting old ones.

**Changes to the initial spec:**
- **Already one shared expert** (`num_shared_experts=1`, width 768), so no merge is needed.
- **The shared expert is the small side.** Per layer it has ~0.8M parameters against ~100M routed (~150M in the full-write layers 4–5). Only the common, low-rank part of the routed output can move into it, not facts. Growing it would densify d512, so it stays at 768.
- **"Pull shared toward routed" (`‖s − sg(r)‖²`) settles at `s = r`.** Both paths then hold the same function and nothing is freed. This batch tests two forms that do free the routed side (`y = s + r`, `sg` = stop-gradient):
  - **Transfer:** `λ‖s − sg(s + r)‖² / sg(‖y‖²)`. Its gradient moves only the shared expert, along the routed output. The shared expert is evaluated a second time on a stop-gradient input, so no gradient reaches the layers below. The LM loss then sheds the overshoot from the routed side. It stops when the routed output has nothing left the shared expert can express.
  - **Routed penalty:** `λ‖r‖² / sg(‖y‖²)`. Routed output is costly, so the LM gradient moves onto the shared expert whatever it can express. The penalty also reaches the layers below, but only in direction, because the routed input is RMS-normalized.
- **Measured first:** a detached width-768 shadow MLP per layer learns `sg(x) → sg(r)` with no effect on training. Its R² is how much of the routed output a shared-sized expert could absorb.

| run | change |
|---|---|
| `shadow` | shadow probe only (all runs carry it) |
| `xfer01` | transfer, λ = 0.01 per layer |
| `xfer04` | transfer, λ = 0.04 per layer |
| `rpen01` | routed penalty, λ = 0.01 per layer |

**Early read** (`shadow`, step 572):

| layer | shadow R² | routed share ‖r‖²/‖y‖² | cos(s, r) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.69 | 0.49 | +0.33 |
| 1 | 0.52 | 0.74 | +0.27 |
| 2 | 0.44 | 0.71 | +0.22 |
| 3 | 0.55 | 0.60 | +0.27 |
| 4 | 0.35 | 0.71 | +0.23 |
| 5 | 0.43 | 0.67 | +0.20 |

- A shared-sized MLP reproduces 35–69% of the routed output, so there's plenty to compress.
- The routed side carries most of the MLP output.
- The two paths already partly duplicate each other: cos(s, r) is positive in every layer.

**Reads:** Paloma macro vs the candidate 11 equal-steps controls (2.9621 / 2.9669, rerun 2.9625; noise 0.0056); cos(s, r), routed share and shadow R² over training. Anything that clears noise gets seed 1, early-fact retention from the fact probe, and an overtrained check.

**Ops:**
- **Lost gradient fixed:** the AttnRes recompute backward dropped every gradient from per-layer stats, so a loss added there was silently ignored. It now passes the compress term's gradient through.
- **Sharded-autotuning deadlock:** new fusions deadlocked sharded XLA autotuning in the train step, because the per-process autotune caches disagree. Turning sharded autotuning off instead hung the first step, likely from mismatched collective order. `--fresh-autotune-cache` starts every process empty, so all miss alike.


**Results** (Paloma macro, seed 0; control = the two shadow-only runs, 2.9633 / 2.9631, mean 2.9632; candidate 11 controls 2.9621 / 2.9625)

| run | loss | Δ | routed share, late | cos(s, r), late |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shadow` (control) | 2.9632 | — | 0.52–0.62 | +0.17 to +0.29 |
| transfer λ = 0.01 | 2.9634 | +0.0002 | 0.23–0.32 | +0.18 to +0.29 |
| transfer λ = 0.04 | 2.9700 | +0.0068 | 0.21–0.38 | +0.16 to +0.32 |
| transfer λ = 0.16 | 2.9745 | +0.0113 | 0.39–0.56 | +0.32 to +0.40 |
| gap `‖s − sg(r)‖²` λ = 0.04 | 2.9679 | +0.0047 | 0.47–0.58 | +0.47 to +0.63 |
| gap λ = 0.16 | 2.9711 | +0.0079 | 0.46–0.59 | +0.49 to +0.66 |
| routed penalty λ = 0.01 | 3.0078 | +0.0446 | 0.01–0.31 | 0.00 to +0.14 |
| routed penalty λ = 0.04 | 3.0070 | +0.0438 | 0.03–0.12 | +0.03 to +0.07 |

- **Closed at d512.** Moving routed work onto the shared expert never helps. Every form strong enough to change behavior costs loss.
- **The shadow probe does nothing to training** (2.9632 vs 2.9621 / 2.9625).
- **Transfer works mechanically but buys nothing.**
  - At λ = 0.01 the routed share halves and the shadow's R² drops ~45%, so the routed side keeps mostly what a shared-sized expert can't express. Loss is unchanged.
  - Stronger weights don't move more. They spend the shared expert's fixed-size MuonH updates chasing the routed output, and loss rises with λ.
- **The gap loss duplicates, as predicted.** cos(s, r) roughly doubles while the routed share barely moves, and loss rises.
- **The routed penalty is destructive even at λ = 0.01.** It shrinks the routed path in every layer, almost entirely in layer 4 (share 0.01). The routed bank does work the shared expert can't take over.
- **Reading:** in the 8-minute regime the routed bank isn't short of space, and the shared expert is already fully used. The capacity argument could still hold when overtrained, but nothing here points to a gain to carry over.
- **Ops: the sharded-autotuning deadlock is unsolved.** Programs with new fusions deadlock in compile about half the time on 8 processes. Every rank waits on the key-value exchange for results no rank publishes. Neither an empty per-process cache nor `xla_gpu_autotune_level=0` fixes it; level 0 instead hangs the first step, inside the lazy custom-kernel load. Resubmitting works, since runs that compile train normally.

🤖 **Batch 179: MLP compression at 100× overtraining** (candidate 11, d512, 281,700 steps = 100× the 2817 equal steps, seed 0; cw-us-east-02a, production priority; [`d5b9ee4eba`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/d5b9ee4eba))

**Why:** in batch 178, moving routed work onto the shared expert did nothing at 2817 steps, or cost loss once it was strong enough to change behavior. The capacity argument says the routed experts only run short of room when overtrained, so this tests the two most informative forms at 100× the tokens.

| run | change |
|---|---|
| `ot100-base` | shadow probe only (control) |
| `ot100-xfer04` | transfer `λ‖s − sg(s + r)‖²`, λ = 0.04 (+0.0068 at 1×) |
| `ot100-gap16` | gap `λ‖s − sg(r)‖²`, λ = 0.16 (+0.0079 at 1×) |

- **Data:** 148B tokens from the 124B-token cache. The loader restarts at the end, so the last ~19% repeats data.
- **Checkpoints:** rolling checkpoints every 20 minutes to the temporary bucket, so a failure resumes. Permanent checkpoint is the final step only.
- **Reads:** Paloma at the midpoint and end vs `ot100-base`; routed share, cos(s, r) and shadow R² over training. Does the compressible share of the routed output, or the gap between arms, move as the run goes on?
- **Timing:** ~4.7 steps/s, ~17 h each.
